subject: Literature
title: Kazuo Ishiguro's Never Let Me Go
description: One-minute skill: Kazuo Ishiguro's Never Let Me Go.

hook.text: Never Let Me Go reads like a gentle English boarding school novel — until you realize what the students are being raised for.

buildup.text: Ishiguro gradually reveals that the students at Hailsham are clones, raised to donate their organs until they die.

discovery.text: The horror is not violence or rebellion. It is the quiet acceptance with which the clones surrender to their fate.

twist.text: There are no villains. Society simply decided that some lives are worth less, and everyone, including the clones, agreed.

climax.text: Ishiguro's dystopia is terrifying because it shows how easily humans normalize exploitation when it benefits them.

punchline.text: The cruelest dystopia is the one nobody fights against.

quiz.question: What makes Never Let Me Go's dystopia uniquely horrifying?
options: The violent oppression of the clone population
The quiet acceptance with which the clones surrender to their fate
The advanced technology used to control minds
